paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God is holy, and He tells us how to come near Him. Nadab and Abihu offered fire "contrary to His command," and that's the heart of it (Leviticus 10:1). They didn't come to God His way, they came their own way. Moses reminds Aaron what the LORD had said: "To those who come near Me I will show My holiness" (Leviticus 10:3).

This is a heavy passage, and I won't pretend it isn't. But look at what God does next: He tells Aaron that the priests must "distinguish between the holy and the common," so they can teach the people His statutes (Leviticus 10:10-11). God wants His people to know Him, and He wants them to know how to draw near. Coming close to Him is a gift, and He gives us the way in so we can walk it with Him.

And here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, baker. I think Aaron's last answer shows a man still trying to honor the LORD on the hardest day of his life, and when Moses heard it, "he was satisfied" (Leviticus 10:19-20). So how do we come near? We listen first, then we follow what He says, even when our own way looks fine, because an oven doesn't care how sincere I am, only whether I read the recipe.
